title: Continue-link upsert-failure abort answers 200 ok:false while the claim DB failure one branch below answers 500 — and the module's own doc only documents the 500
detail: Two server-side DB failures in one handler get different status conventions (200-with-ok:false vs 500), and handle_save_draft's identical upsert failure is also 500 (line 219). The client treats 500 and ok:false identically (catch -> CONTINUE_FAILED), so the 200 buys nothing and hides the failure from status-based monitoring. The no-oracle rationale covers claim outcomes, not DB errors.
recommended_fix: Return wisp.internal_server_error() from the upsert-abort arm (matching the claim arm and handle_save_draft), or document why this one DB failure deliberately stays 200.

title: strip_draft_on_submit.sql manually SETs updated_at = now() — dead code the BEFORE UPDATE trigger overwrites, contradicting the migration's stated convention and the four sibling draft UPDATEs
evidence:
UPDATE application_draft
SET fields = '{}'::jsonb,
    continue_token = NULL,
    submitted_at = now(),
    updated_at = now()
WHERE vacancy_id = $1::uuid
  AND email = lower($2)
RETURNING id::text;

-- migration 20260802120000_create_application_draft.sql states:
-- updated_at follows the repo's trigger convention (update_updated_at_column
-- from 20260409000001_add_ai_analysis_updated_at.sql), not manual SETs.
detail: The update_application_draft_updated_at trigger fires on every UPDATE and overwrites updated_at, so the manual SET is dead weight. claim/clear/erase/mark_resumed draft UPDATEs all rely on the trigger; strip is the lone outlier, inviting future readers to doubt the trigger covers this table.
recommended_fix: Drop the updated_at = now() line from strip_draft_on_submit.sql and regenerate via Squirrel; the trigger owns the stamp.
